solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Highland player's defeat at the last moment in front of Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: says the first piece goes before the second in the answer

parts.note: to pip someone (at the post) is to beat them right at the finish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A Scottish musician's narrow loss, suffered before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeat at the last moment' reads like a scoreline, but it is the verb pip, as in 'pipped at the post'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes, the instrument associated with the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Make detailed proposal for extraterrestrial orbiter

parts.note: to plan is to set out a detailed proposal
ET is the familiar abbreviation for an extraterrestrial, as in the film

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a scheme for an alien spacecraft circling a world.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a body that orbits a star, so it is an orbiter.

clue.text: Painting to me is all about natural colouring

indicators.note: something all about, scattered every which way, has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An artist declaring that their work is all about the colours of nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is all about' shuffles the twelve letters of PAINTING TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigmentation is the colour of skin, leaves or fur given by natural pigments.

clue.text: Eritrean working as servant

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Eritrea employed in domestic service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ERITREAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an old word for a household servant or attendant.

clue.text: Tyrant with the ultimate in vileness in store

indicators.note: puts the chosen letter inside the word for store

parts.note: a depot is a store or warehouse

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last one, here taken from vileness

explanation.surface: A tyrant who has the very worst wickedness kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in' gives S, the last letter of 'vileness'; the second 'in' puts it inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who exercises power cruelly, a synonym for tyrant.

clue.text: Top film award for Mark

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award for films

explanation.surface: The leading prize in cinema goes to someone named Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb here: behead OSCAR to leave its last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Bookseller, say, turning up A Study in Scarlet?

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a study is a piece of art, a drawing made as practice

explanation.surface: A bookshop owner unearthing a copy of Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses REDART, read with 'in' as a link joining the pieces, giving TRA + DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookseller is one example of a trader, someone who buys and sells goods, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Sexier crew mostly worked out — this improves muscles

indicators.note: letters worked out are reshaped into a new order
most of a word, so the final letter of crew is dropped

explanation.surface: A rowing crew getting sexier by working out in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CREW to CRE; 'worked out' rearranges SEXIER plus CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exerciser is a piece of gym equipment used to build strength in the body.

clue.text: Marksman notes what could be owl

parts.note: sharps are musical notes raised a semitone
an owl hoots, so it could be called a hooter

explanation.surface: A marksman's jottings about what might be an owl in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is an expert shot with a gun, a synonym for marksman.

clue.text: Dread flying gnats

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a new order

explanation.surface: Fear of a swarm of airborne insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges GNATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep anxiety or dread, borrowed from German.

clue.text: Hinders Cockney with division of M&S

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: hampers means hinders
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A Londoner obstructing a branch of Marks & Spencer, the British high-street store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the H of HAMPERS. The definition is cryptic: the & symbol sits between M and S, dividing them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the name of the & sign, which separates the two letters in M&S.

clue.text: What's among finite numbers?

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question asking which values count as finite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' hides the answer across 'finiTE Numbers'; the whole clue is also the definition, since ten is one of the finite numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is an ordinary whole number, so it is certainly one of the finite numbers.

clue.text: Tape prone to tangle as a medium for messages

indicators.note: tangled letters are knotted into a different order

explanation.surface: Sticky tape that keeps snarling up, used to send messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tangle' rearranges TAPE PRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepaper is writing paper on which letters and short notes are written.

clue.text: Expecting ruling to follow pressure

indicators.note: says the ruling word comes after the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the standard symbol for pressure in physics
regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: Anticipating a court ruling once pressure has been applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts REGNANT after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is an everyday idiom for being pregnant, awaiting a baby.

clue.text: What can sweep up as it races around?

indicators.note: letters moved around are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that brushes upward while dashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges AS IT RACES. 'Sweep up' means rise in a grand curve, not clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand staircase is often described as sweeping up, rising in a broad curve to the floor above.

clue.text: Fast dog is in view

indicators.note: says the dog word sits inside the word for view

parts.note: to see is to view
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A speedy dog comes into sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast', not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly fixed, so fast and secure are synonyms.

clue.text: Fuss surrounding a US soldier's movement

indicators.note: the fuss word wraps around the pieces that follow

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A commotion around an American serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is the musical sense: a section of a longer work.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement of a symphony or sonata, a piece of music.

clue.text: Fashionable joint

definitions.meaning: the joint between the leg and pelvis

explanation.surface: A trendy bar or nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip means stylish in slang, and the hip is the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the leg.

clue.text: Quiet ending dropped by Domingo, perhaps

indicators.note: the final letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Plácido Domingo is the opera tenor, so Domingo is one person called Placido

explanation.surface: A singer going silent at the end of an aria.
explanation.walkthrough: Domingo is the surname of the tenor Plácido Domingo; 'ending dropped by' removes the last letter of his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and peaceful, so quiet in temperament.

clue.text: Leader that is getting newspaper into row

indicators.note: getting, with into, says the pieces are put inside the word for row
into, after getting, says the pieces go inside the word for row

parts.note: a chain is a row or series of linked things
ie, id est, is Latin for that is
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A head of an organisation drawing a newspaper into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of linked things.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the leader of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Thin metal sword

definitions.meaning: metal beaten into a very thin sheet

explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen foil is thinly rolled metal, and the foil is one of the three fencing weapons.

clue.text: Room under roof in Bugatti cabriolet

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the letters of the car's name

explanation.surface: A vintage open-topped Bugatti stored up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the answer across 'BugATTI Cabriolet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space or room just below the roof of a house.

clue.text: Interpretation of name in right version of text

indicators.note: puts the name letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: an edition is a version of a published text

explanation.surface: A reading of a name found in the correct edition of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside R + EDITION, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation of a song, role or text.

clue.text: Weary being restrained welcoming king

indicators.note: taking a guest in, so the king letter goes inside

parts.note: tied means restrained, bound up
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted from being held back while greeting a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts R inside TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and weary are synonyms for feeling worn out.
